Questions 11–20

Questions 11–15
Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

11. The Seaview Marine Heritage Centre was originally established to
    A. preserve historical fishing vessels.
    B. monitor endangered seal colonies.
    C. provide employment for retired sailors.

12. What change was made to the main exhibition hall last winter?
    A. An interactive touch-screen gallery was installed.
    B. The floor space was doubled in size.
    C. A new café area was added.

13. Visitors are advised that the Coastal Cliff Trail
    A. is unsuitable for pushchairs and wheelchairs.
    B. requires tickets to be booked 24 hours in advance.
    C. is closed whenever the tide is rising.

14. How can families receive a discount on boat excursions?
    A. By presenting a valid rail travel card.
    B. By booking through the official mobile app.
    C. By purchasing combined museum-and-boat tickets.

15. What is the speaker’s recommendation regarding lunch?
    A. Eat at the outdoor picnic benches near the lighthouse.
    B. Reserve a table in advance at the Waterfront Bistro.
    C. Try the traditional seafood chowder at the Harbour Kiosk.

parts.title: Section 3
parts.content:
Questions 21–30

Questions 21–25
Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

21. What is the primary focus of Jack and Chloe’s engineering research project?
    A. Testing lightweight battery storage for domestic solar panels.
    B. Evaluating rooftop vegetable gardens on commercial office blocks.
    C. Comparing the insulating efficiency of extensive green roofs.

22. Why did they decide against conducting their experiments on university campus roofs?
    A. Health and safety regulations prohibited student access.
    B. The roofs had unsuitable drainage systems.
    C. Background noise interfered with their electronic sensors.

23. What problem did Chloe encounter when reviewing previous literature?
    A. Most published studies were conducted in tropical climates.
    B. Sample sizes used in previous trials were too small.
    C. The cost data was outdated and inaccurate.

24. Their tutor advises them that their methodology must include
    A. daily calibration of moisture sensors.
    B. an identical control roof without vegetation.
    C. interviews with building maintenance staff.

25. What unexpected finding emerged from their preliminary temperature data?
    A. Sedum plants provided superior winter insulation to grass turf.
    B. Heat reduction was greatest during windy afternoons.
    C. Roof surface temperatures dropped by up to twelve degrees Celsius.

Questions 26–30
Who will be responsible for completing each of the following project tasks?
Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A, B or C, next to 

Questions 26–30.

    A   Jack
    B   Chloe
    C   Both Jack and Chloe

26. Statistical analysis of humidity logs           ....................
27. Creating digital 3D roof diagrams              ....................
28. Writing the literature review chapter          ....................
29. Preparing presentation slides for the seminar  ....................
30. Proofreading the final research paper          ....................

Anatomy and Cellular Structure:
• Cephalopods (octopuses, squids, and cuttlefish) manipulate skin appearance using specialized cells.
• Chromatophores:
  - Elastic sacs containing pigment granules (yellow, red, brown, black).
  - Controlled directly by radial 31 .................... attached to the central nervous system.
  - Allow rapid pattern shifts in less than a 32 ....................
• Iridophores:
  - Beneath chromatophores; produce metallic hues of gold, green, and 33 ....................
• Leucophores:
  - Act as passive broadband reflectors, producing a bright 34 .................... background.

Tactile Texture Transformation:
• Tiny muscular structures called 35 .................... alter skin texture from smooth to rough or spiky.
• Enables animals to blend into rough kelp, coarse sand, or pitted 36 ....................

Sensory Coordination:
• Along with chromatic aberration, they can detect the 37 .................... of light to notice contrast in open water.
• Recent research indicates skin tissue contains 38 .................... molecules similar to those in retinas, suggesting dermal light reception.

Defensive & Communicative Functions:
• Camouflage offers vital protection from apex marine 39 .................... (e.g. sharks and seals).
• Dynamic 'passing cloud' waves used to startle prey or disorient attackers.
• High-contrast flashing stripes employed during courtship and territorial 40 ....................
